headline: Hochul Taps $200 Million From NYC Transit in ‘Backdoor Raid’
content: (Bloomberg) -- New York Governor Kathy Hochul is using New York City’s public transportation system to help resolve the city’s estimated $6.2 billion budget deficit for next year.The state-run Metropolitan Transportation Authority, which operates the city’s subways, buses and two commuter railroads, will get $200 million less in subsidy payments from the city to fund buses, according to MTA’s financial documents.Reinvent Albany, a fiscal watchdog group, on Monday called the move a “backdoor raid” on the agency’s bus funding. “Unfortunately, the state has quietly chosen not to compensate MTA Bus, leaving the MTA – and ultimately bus riders – to eat the loss of city funding,” Reinvent Albany said in its statement.On Wednesday, the MTA is set to update its own projected budget deficits for future years. In its July financial plan, the MTA said the one-time $200 million cut in the bus subsidy would be covered by its own resources. “Despite the reduction in City reimbursement, the MTA Plan continues to provide the resources necessary to maintain current bus service levels for customers,” it said in the plan. The city is on the hook for a $732.7 million bus subsidy payment to the MTA in 2026, and a $674.5 million bus subsidy payment in 2027, according to the agency’s financial documents. Meanwhile, New York City officials are projecting a $6.2 billion deficit for the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2027, with that gap potentially increasing to nearly $9 billion in fiscal year 2030, according to city documents. Using the MTA’s budget to help support other spending in the state has happened before. Former Governor Andrew Cuomo redirected millions of dollars from the MTA’s operating budget during his tenure to the state’s spending plan. New York’s Governor nominates the MTA’s chief executive officer and board chair.Hochul has found new funding resources for the MTA in the past, including raising the payroll mobility tax on certain businesses to help support the transit network once federal pandemic aid money ended. “No Governor has stepped up to support the MTA and its riders like Governor Hochul,” said Sean Butler, a spokesperson for the governor, in an emailed statement. “She saved the agency from a fiscal cliff and has made historic investments to improve and expand service. Allowing a reduction in NYC’s FY27 subsidy of MTA bus service was part of a comprehensive package to address the City’s deficit and has zero impact on bus service for New Yorkers.”The MTA already has its own budget gaps to fix. It anticipates a $295 million deficit in 2027 that is expected to grow to nearly $900 million by 2030. MTA officials are set to update those budget projections on Wednesday during the agency’s monthly board meeting. More stories like this are available on bloomberg.com©2026 Bloomberg L.P.

headline: VHP warns against repeal of anti-conversion, anti-cow slaughter laws in Karnataka
content: MANGALURU The Vishva Hindu Parishad (VHP) warned of organising massive protests and a public movement across Karnataka if the State Government decides to withdraw or weaken the anti-conversion law and the anti-cow slaughter law. Religious minority leaders urge Karnataka government to repeal anti-conversion law, strengthen legislation to address hate speech storyline 1 Addressing press persons in Udupi on November 16, K. R. Sunil, Working President of Udupi district unit of VHP, said that the Karnataka Protection of Right to Freedom of Religion Act, 2022 and the Karnataka Prevention of Slaughter and Preservation of Cattle Act, 2020 should not be withdrawn under any circumstance during the upcoming winter session of the State legislature in Belagavi. Winter Session in Belagavi starting Dec. 2 storyline 1 “The organisation urges the government not to attempt to weaken these laws,” he said. Contradictions within India’s cow protection regime Contradictions within India’s cow protection regime Politics and sentiment continue to overshadow realities of cattle preservation in India Contradictions within India’s cow protection regime opinion 1 Mr. Sunil said the State Government should not yield to the pressure exerted by certain organisations demanding repeal of these two laws. He condemned the statement by Karnataka Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) President B. K. Hariprasad regarding the potential withdrawal of the anti-conversion law during the Belagavi session, which is set to begin on December 2. Also Read: Pressure rising on Karnataka government to withdraw anti-cow slaughter and anti-conversion laws https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/karnataka/pressure-on-karnataka-government-to-withdraw-anti-cow-slaughter-and-anti-conversion-laws-increasing/article71546754.ece “The anti-conversion law does not target any specific religion. Instead, it aims to prevent unlawful conversions that occur through force, fraud, inducement, or misrepresentation. The Supreme Court has clarified in a past judgment that forced conversion is not a fundamental right. Since a Congress government in Himachal Pradesh has implemented such a law, any attempt to repeal it in Karnataka is inappropriate,” he said. “Cattle are the backbone of the Indian agricultural system. Therefore, the anti-cow slaughter law is essential for protecting the interests of farmers and preserving livestock. This legislation has aided in the protection of cattle within the State and has helped curb illegal cattle transportation and theft,” he said adding, “Any attempt to weaken this law for the sake of political appeasement could lead to unnecessary communal conflict.” ‘Military training’ opposed The VHP also opposed a tender floated by the State Government’s Directorate of Minorities to provide 60 days of military (army) training exclusively to students from minority communities for the year 2026-27. BJP leader Ravi Kumar seeks withdrawal of ‘army training’ advertisement by Minorities Department of Karnataka storyline 1 “Using public tax funds to provide training solely to students from one community, while excluding eligible, underprivileged students from other communities, runs counter to the constitutional principle of equality. This tender be cancelled immediately,” he said. The VHP will submit memoranda on the three matters to the Governor, Chief Minister, and the Chief Secretary through the Deputy Commissioner and tahsildars, he said.

headline: Census 2027: Self-enumeration for second phase starts in poll-bound States
content: New Delhi The self-enumeration for the second phase of the Census 2027 kicked off on Monday (November 16, 2026) for Goa, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh and the non-snow-bound areas of Uttarakhand — States where Assembly polls are due early next year. Residents can use a special website created for the purpose — se.census.gov.in — to fill their details till November 30 for population enumeration, according to a statement issued by the government. https://se.census.gov.in/ States asked to flag data quality concerns, make corrections in real time during Census 2027 States asked to flag data quality concerns, make corrections in real time during Census 2027 This is the first digital Census, with enumerators using an app to record data, allowing for monitoring, correction, targeted supervisory intervention; in Phase 1, some enumerators asked to go back, correct data “discrepancies” States asked to flag data quality concerns, make corrections in real time during Census 2027 storyline 1 Once the residents complete the online procedure, a unique Self-Enumeration ID (SE ID) will be generated, which they will have to share with the enumerator during the subsequent field visit to complete the process. "The corresponding house-to-house Population Enumeration in these states and areas will be conducted from December 1, 2026, to January 4, 2027, followed by a revisional round from January 5 to 9, 2027. The reference date for these states/areas will be 00:00 hours of January 5, 2027," the statement said. In the remaining States and Union territories, population enumeration will be conducted from January 25 to February 28, 2027, followed by a revisional round from March 1 to March 5, 2027. The process for Manipur has been put on hold. "The provision for Self-Enumeration in these states/UTs will be available from January 10 to 24, 2027, prior to the commencement of house-to-house visits by enumerators. The reference date for Census in these states/UTs will be 00:00 hours of March 1, 2027," the statement said. Census 2027: What are the new questions, and how are enumerators being trained? | Explained Census 2027: What are the new questions, and how are enumerators being trained? | Explained As Uttar Pradesh and three other poll-bound States — Uttarakhand, Goa and Punjab — prepare to launch the second phase of Census 2027 on December 1, field trainers are briefing about 34 lakh enumerators on 40 questions that will require longer, more sensitive interviews and digital data entry, including caste, religion, Aadhaar access and parents’ details Census 2027: What are the new questions, and how are enumerators being trained? | Explained storyline 1 The first phase of the mammoth headcount exercise — Houselisting and Housing Census (HLO) — has been completed across 35 States and Union territories, except Manipur, it said. The first ever digital exercise in the history of the Census is being done by digital tools, with self-enumeration introduced as an additional facility, handheld devices carried by enumerators and a bespoke software prepared to collect real-time data from the field. "The self-enumeration process is a secure, convenient and user-friendly web-based facility available in 16 Indian languages. To participate in Self-Enumeration during Phase II, residents can log in to the official portal se.census.gov.in using their mobile number (preferably the one registered during Phase I) along with basic details and answer 40 notified questions covering household and individual particulars," the statement said. The population enumeration in Ladakh and the snow-bound non-synchronous areas of Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand took place from September 1 to September 30. Households that do not opt for self-enumeration will be covered during the house-to-house visits by enumerators, the statement said. The information collected under the Census Act, 1948, is strictly confidential and used solely for statistical purposes and development planning, it said.

headline: Sonia Gandhi’s memoir launch: ‘When you are an outsider, you have this feeling of not being like others, of always being watched’
content: If there is a recurring theme in Sonia Gandhi’s life, it is her struggle to belong. To the Italian city of Orbassano near Turin, where she moved with her family from the small Piemontese village of Sangano as a child. To India, where she landed on January 13, 1968, to see for herself the country and the people of the land whose Prime Minister’s son she hoped to marry. To Indian politics, that she was loath to join until circumstances pushed her to it. There was, however, one place where Sonia seemed to belong without having to try: beside the man she had fallen in love with in Cambridge, Rajiv Gandhi. Their love, son and Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi recounted to a packed audience at the launch of Sonia’s memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love (HarperCollins India) in the Capital on Monday evening, was so instinctive that it shaped his very understanding of what a family should look like. “Every meal, there would be Papa and on Papa’s lap, there would be Mamma. I thought this was a normal thing. And I would go to my friend’s house and they wouldn’t be sitting on each other’s laps and I would ask my friends, what is going on? Why is your mother not sitting on your father’s lap… This is what we grew up with,” he said, as the audience burst out in laughter. It was a star-studded launch with top party leaders and Opposition Chief Ministers in attendance. From Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay, J&K Chief Minister Omar Abdullah, Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren, Karnataka Chief Minister D K Shivakumar and Himachal Pradesh Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu to Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav and wife Dimple Yadav, NCP (SP)’s Supriya Sule, National Conference chief Farooq Abdullah, TMC's Abhishek Banerjee, and even BJP leader Amarinder Singh. Also present were Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, Jairam Ramesh, Mani Shankar Aiyar, Sachin Pilot, former Prime Minister Manmohan Singh's wife Gursharan Kaur, Sonia's children Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, the latter with husband Robert Vadra and children Raihan and Miraya. Before Rahul’s speech, in a discussion with HarperCollins publisher Poulomi Chatterjee, Sonia spoke of how it was at the behest of Rahul and Priyanka that she had finally decided to write of her tumultuous and storied life. “Many people have told me over the years that you must write your story. But I have always been very reticent to disclose my inner feelings and what I think about things and people and places,” said Sonia, 79. Belonging spans the arc of her life, from her childhood in Italy to meeting and marrying Rajiv Gandhi to adjusting to her life in India and her entry into politics after the assassination of her husband. It is a revealing glimpse into the private world of a woman who would go on to become one of India’s most influential political leaders. "Sonia Gandhi’s memoir is a bold and frank account of her life, written from the heart. When President Abdul Kalam invited her to be the Prime Minister, she declined what no leader in the world, male or female, would have done. This was not a small thing. The fact is that had the Congress party continued under Sitaram Kesri, it would have collapsed. The Congress party can only prosper and grow if a Gandhi leads them,” said CM Shivakumar. For grandson Raihan Vadra, 26, it was, however, not her political life alone that was of interest. “I had read the manuscript while she was writing it. But what I found most interesting were the stories of her childhood in Italy. I hadn’t known a lot of those stories, so they were a revelation to me,” he said. For former Lok Sabha Speaker Meira Kumar, it was the story of deep love that had drawn Sonia to India and the extraordinary sacrifices she had made that makes Belonging a memoir worth reading. "I have just begun reading the book but I am struck by their love story. As Rahul said, they (Sonia and Rajiv) truly belonged to each other," she said. Since the publication of the book on November 10, Belonging has already sold 200,000 copies. “It is a properly good book. The Indira years and the extraordinary details Mrs Gandhi packs in the memoir makes it a literary treat. Her visit to Ananda Bhawan is, I think, one of the best bits in the memoir,” said Chiki Sarkar, publisher, Juggernaut. In the book as well as at the launch, Sonia insisted on keeping politics in the background. Instead she spoke of feeling at home. Just as she has embraced India, India too, has embraced her as its own: “When you are an outsider, you have this feeling of not being like others, of always being watched. I felt that I truly belonged when I visited my husband's constituency for the first time. People in villages are much more frank and outright, unlike city people. They didn’t care if my accent was strange, if my sari wasn’t tied the right way as long as I was there to speak to them, to ask about their lives, to hear of their problems… They would even scold me, tell me to shut up, aap chup raho, aap yaha nahi rahte hain, aapko kuch nahin maloom. Hum log tay karenge. That too was acceptance,” she said. Would there be a sequel to her book? “I am happy my mother finally got to tell her story in her own words, you will have to ask my mother about that,” said Priyanka.

headline: I.N.D.I.A. bloc leaders, Tamil Nadu CM Vijay, BJP’s Amarinder Singh attend Sonia Gandhi's book launch
content: <p>New Delhi: Several I.N.D.I.A. bloc leaders, including Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav and TMC’s Abhishek Banerjee, Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay and BJP leader Amarinder Singh attended the launch of Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson <a href="https://www.deccanherald.com/tags/sonia-gandhi">Sonia Gandhi</a>'s memoir here on Monday.</p>.<p>Published by HarperCollins India, ‘<a href="https://www.deccanherald.com/india/her-book-should-have-been-called-whitewashing-bjp-says-sonia-gandhi-tried-to-justify-emergency-in-memoir-4213523">Belonging: A Journey of Love</a>’ was released last Tuesday to a lot of enthusiasm from readers, who have been lining up at prominent bookstores to pick up copies of the memoir while many have been ordering it online.</p>.<p>Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, former party chief Rahul Gandhi and AICC general secretary Priyanka Gandhi Vadra were present at the official launch event at the ITC Maurya.</p>.'Desi beti' vs 'videshi bahu': Sonia Gandhi recalls 1999 Bellary battle.<p>Other than Vijay, Akhilesh Yadav and Banerjee, Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren, J&K Chief Minister Omar Abdullah, National Conference chief Farooq Abdullah, NCP (SP) leader Supriya Sule, BJP leader and ex-Punjab chief minister Amarinder Singh, Congress chief ministers D K Shivakumar (Karnataka) and Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu (Himachal Pradesh) also attended the launch event, along with several senior Congress leaders.</p>.<p>While the BJP has accused Sonia Gandhi of "whitewashing" events in the book, Congress leaders have hailed the memoir as candid and lauded the former party chief for her achievements.</p>.<p>‘Belonging: A Journey of Love’ is a personal memoir, with politics providing the background or “a kind of framework”, she writes in the book.</p>

headline: Andhra’s proposed Investment Protection Act seeks to shield investors from policy U-turns
content: VIJAYAWADA The Investment Protection Act (IPA) proposed to be enacted by the Andhra Pradesh government is being considered as a legislative intervention which the State desperately needs, given the bitter experiences of the past, when certain policy reversals unravelled the good work that was done. https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/andhra-pradesh/andhra-to-bring-in-investment-protection-act-to-ease-doing-business-says-naidu/article71693742.ece https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/andhra-pradesh/ It will also enable the government to deal with extraneous factors that could jeopardise investments. https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/andhra-pradesh/andhra-pradesh-secures-988-lakh-crore-investment-commitments-at-cii-partnership-summit-in-vizag/article71699029.ece As of November 16, such a move to protect investments is unprecedented as no other State or even the Central government has such legislation. Andhra Pradesh secures ₹9.88 lakh crore investment commitments at CII Partnership Summit in Vizag Andhra Pradesh secures ₹9.88 lakh crore investment commitments at CII Partnership Summit in Vizag A.P. government will implement Investment Protection Act with retrospective effect from 2024, says Chief Minister Naidu Andhra Pradesh secures ₹9.88 lakh crore investment commitments at CII Partnership Summit in Vizag storyline 1 The ‘three capitals’ fiasco, the review of long-term Renewable Energy (RE) Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs) and the shifting of a massive battery manufacturing plant from Andhra Pradesh to Mahabubnagar in Telangana in 2019-24, purportedly due to the vindictive attitude of the then government, are a few major setbacks suffered by the State. https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/andhra-pradesh/three-capitals-petitions-infructuous-now-that-amaravati-is-andhras-capital-by-law-high-court-says/article71511718.ece https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/telangana/ When such regressive actions are taken, the courts might resolve the disputes. What the State government intends to do by bringing in the IPA is to prevent the damage instead of fire-fighting later. Three-capitals petitions infructuous now that Amaravati is Andhra’s capital by law, High Court says Three-capitals petitions infructuous now that Amaravati is Andhra’s capital by law, High Court says Full Bench posts pending matters to November 20, ahead of the Supreme Court’s likely hearing on November 29 of the appeals against the High Court’s 2022 Amaravati judgment Three-capitals petitions infructuous now that Amaravati is Andhra’s capital by law, High Court says storyline 1 Regarding Amaravati, the High Court ruled on March 3, 2022 that the government of the day headed by the YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) had no legislative competence to shift or split the capital. But, not wanting to take a chance, the present government went on to secure legal sanctity for Amaravati as the permanent capital of Andhra Pradesh by having the A.P. Reorganisation Act, 2014 amended by Parliament. https://www.thehindu.com/topic/yuvajana-sramika-rythu-congress-party/ https://www.thehindu.com/opinion/editorial/balance-is-key-on-the-andhra-pradesh-reorganisation-amendment-bill-and-amaravati/article70826878.ece There is no such law at the moment that can guarantee the safety of investments being made in the State, which prompted Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu to devise the IPA and pass it in the upcoming session of the Legislative Assembly. The review of RE PPAs in July 2019, which happened in spite of a caution by the Union Ministry of Power, was a major controversy that cast a shadow on potential investments. It was a signal that political regime changes could lead to retroactive cancellation of legal agreements. How did the ‘Amaravati Bill’ come into place? How did the ‘Amaravati Bill’ come into place? Why has Amaravati been declared the sole capital of A.P.? Why did the A.P. Reorganisation Act need to be amended? How did the ‘Amaravati Bill’ come into place? storyline 1 The above policy decisions have lowered investor confidence and dented the State’s Ease of Doing Business framework. The IPA seeks to pre-empt all such possible damage. P.V.G. Umesh Chandra, an advocate in the Andhra Pradesh High Court, told The Hindu that the IPA was specifically intended to curb the ‘arbitrary menace’ of overturning of laws passed by a particular government, thereby boosting the much-needed investor confidence. Constitutional courts have deprecated the practice of arbitrary and malafide change of policies for which no legal reasons were rendered, he noted, while implying that the IPA was aimed at safeguarding investments across the State mainly including in Amaravati. Explained | Andhra Pradesh’s capital conundrum Explained | Andhra Pradesh’s capital conundrum Why did the 2014 TDP government decide on Amaravati as the capital city? What is the Andhra Pradesh CRDA Act? What is the current Chief Minister’s plan with respect to a capital city? EXPLAINER Explained | Andhra Pradesh’s capital conundrum storyline 1 The State has the power to enact the IPA as such a power falls under Entry 20 (economic and social planning) of the Concurrent List in the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution, he added. Confederation of Indian Industry - AP Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) Andhra Pradesh chairman S. Narendra Kumar said the IPA would help in attracting more investments to the State as the confidence in the investor community would go up, and acknowledged that it was essential to prevent the flight of capital likely to be caused by hostile business environments. A central law to protect Amaravati A central law to protect Amaravati The move follows years of political turmoil surrounding the capital STATE OF PLAY A central law to protect Amaravati opinion 1

headline: 2 suspicious boxes found near Anupgarh rail track following information from Nov 3 blast accused
content: Police on Monday found two suspicious boxes near a railway track in Rajasthan's Anupgarh district after the two accused arrested in connection with the November 3 railway track blast claimed that they had planted bombs in the area."The suspicious objects were found near a 'mazar' close to the Ramsinghpur-Anupgarh railway track. The area has been cordoned off the area and bomb disposal squad has been informed," a police official said.Police are awaiting examination of the objects by the bomb disposal squad to establish whether they contain explosives.The officer said that the accused had disclosed during questioning that they had also planted bombs in the area on October 12-13."When we went to verify the information, we found two suspicious boxes that appeared to be bombs," he said."We have restricted public movement in the area and informed the bomb disposal squad and railway authorities," the officer said.The development comes a day after Rajasthan Police announced the arrest of Mahakdeep Kaur and Devendra Singh from Punjab's Gurdaspur district in connection with the November 3 blast on the railway track in the Ramsinghpur police station area.The blast occurred about 45 minutes after a passenger train had passed through the area. The explosion created a crater about two feet deep between the rails.The arrests were made on November 14 during a joint operation by Rajasthan ATS, Sri Ganganagar police, Punjab Counter Intelligence and Gurdaspur police.According to police, preliminary investigation indicated that the accused were allegedly acting on instructions from Pakistan-based handlers.Investigators had earlier said the accused attempted to plant a timer bomb on the railway track on October 12-13, but the device failed to explode due to a technical defect.Police said the November 3 explosion was carried out using another time bomb allegedly supplied by a Pakistan-based handler.The two accused are being questioned to ascertain the involvement of other persons and the extent of the suspected network.

headline: Supreme Court rejects plea against Maharashtra's rotation policy for reserved SC/ST seats in local bodies
content: New Delhi The Supreme Court on Monday (November 16, 2026) refused to entertain a plea challenging a provision in the Maharashtra government's rules that treats the general elections to Zila Parishads and Panchayat Samitis after the enforcement of the rules as the first for the rotation of reserved seats for Scheduled Castes (SC) and Scheduled Tribes (ST). A Bench comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana dismissed an appeal filed by Sau. Rupali Indrabhushan Sonde against the September 19, 2025, judgment of the Nagpur Bench of the Bombay High Court, saying, "No voter or a candidate can have a vested right to have a constituency declared as a reserved seat for SCs or STs." The bench said such decisions fall under the policy domain, and the petitioner cannot say that the rotation policy has to be exercised in a particular manner. The bench, however, took note of the submissions of senior advocate Vipin Sanghi, appearing for Sonde, and permitted the petitioner to file a representation to the Maharashtra government for reconsideration of the rules related to the reservation of seats for SCs and STs under the rotation policy for local body elections. On September 19, 2025, a division bench comprising Justices Rajnish R. Vyas and Anil S. Kilor of the Bombay High Court dismissed a batch of petitions challenging the provision in the Maharashtra government's 2025 rules. It had held that the petitioners failed to establish that the introduction of Rule XII of the Maharashtra Zilla Parishads and Panchayat Samitis (Manner and Rotation of Reservation of Seats) Rules, 2025, was arbitrary or unconstitutional. "(XII) First Election for rotation: For rotation of seats under these Rules, the general election held after commencement of these Rules shall be considered as the first election," the impugned rule reads. The plea challenged Rule XII, stating that the provision would disrupt the existing reservation rotation system and adversely affect candidates seeking to contest elections from reserved constituencies. It was argued before the high court that the new rule was arbitrary, violated Article 14 of the Constitution and exceeded the scope of the parent Maharashtra Zilla Parishads and Panchayat Samitis Act, 1961. The petitioners had also maintained that the right to contest elections would be affected by resetting the rotation process. Opposing the petitions, the State government had said that the rules had been framed to give effect to Section 12 of the 1961 Act, particularly after the amendment that empowered it, with the approval of the State Election Commission, to divide districts into electoral divisions. The government had pointed out that the boundaries of electoral constituencies were being changed for the first time under the revised exercise. As a result, the geographical composition of constituencies, population distribution and reservation status could also change, it had said. While acknowledging that the principle of rotation must be respected, the High Court had held that earlier judgments relied upon by the petitioners were distinguishable because the present case involved a fresh delimitation exercise undertaken under Section 12(1) of the Act.

headline: Himachal Pradesh: 12 Tourists Injured as Vehicle Plunges into Gorge in Kullu
content: Twelve tourists hailing from Odisha sustained injuries when the Tempo Traveller they were travelling in skidded off the road and fell approximately 20 metres into a gorge near Sarsadi on the Bhuntar-Manikaran road in Himachal Pradesh's Kullu district on Monday.Information was available with The Chenab Times that the injured individuals were promptly transported to the Regional Hospital in Kullu. Their conditions are reported to be out of danger.The group of tourists was en route to the pilgrimage site of Manikaran when the vehicle reportedly veered off the road abruptly, leading to the accident. Local residents and the police initiated immediate rescue operations following the incident.The Superintendent of Police (SP) for Kullu, Abhishek Sekar, confirmed that an investigation has been launched to determine the precise cause of the accident. The route connecting Bhuntar and Manikaran is known for its scenic beauty but also presents challenging terrain, with narrow stretches and steep gradients, particularly in areas prone to landslides.Manikaran, a popular destination situated in the Parvati Valley, attracts a significant number of tourists throughout the year. It is revered for its hot springs and Gurudwara sahib, as well as its proximity to trekking routes and natural landscapes. The accessibility to Manikaran is primarily via the Bhuntar-Manikaran road, which often requires careful navigation by drivers.Accidents involving tourist vehicles are not uncommon in the hilly regions of Himachal Pradesh, often attributed to factors such as driver fatigue, adverse weather conditions, road quality, and the challenging topography. Authorities in the state regularly issue advisories to tourists and local taxi operators regarding safe driving practices in mountainous areas.The injured tourists were travelling as part of a larger group undertaking a religious and recreational tour of the region. The tempo traveller, a common mode of transport for group excursions, was carrying the occupants when the incident occurred. The specific circumstances leading to the vehicle losing control are under scrutiny by the police.Rescue efforts involved local villagers who were quick to respond to the sound of the crash, followed by the arrival of police personnel. The process of extricating the injured from the damaged vehicle and ensuring their swift transfer to medical facilities was a priority for the responders. The prompt medical attention provided at the Regional Hospital in Kullu is understood to have played a crucial role in stabilizing the condition of the injured tourists.The Kullu district administration has reiterated its commitment to ensuring the safety of tourists and has pledged full cooperation with the ongoing investigation. Officials are expected to review the road conditions and traffic management protocols along the Bhuntar-Manikaran route in light of this incident. While the exact cause remains under investigation, preliminary reports suggest a potential loss of control on a curve.The incident highlights the inherent risks associated with travel in mountainous terrains and underscores the importance of adherence to traffic regulations and safe driving practices. Further details are awaited as the police continue their investigation into the accident that has led to injuries among the visitors from Odisha.

headline: NABARD brings the best of rural India to Shimla
content: Shimla, 16 November 2026: The National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD), Himachal Pradesh Regional Office, is organising the Grameen Bharat Mahotsav (GBM) – Himachal Pradesh 2026 at the Padamdev Complex, The Ridge, Shimla, from 19 to 28 November 2026. Rural artisans, weavers, Self Help Groups (SHGs), Joint Liability Groups (JLGs), Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs) and Off-Farm Producer Organisations (OFPOs) from 10 states will display and sell their products at 40 stalls. Dr. Vivek Pathania, Chief General Manager, NABARD Himachal Pradesh Regional Office, will inaugurate the Mahotsav on 19 November 2026 at 12.00 PM. "Grameen Bharat Mahotsav lets our rural producers sell directly to customers. When they meet buyers face to face, they earn better prices, learn what the market wants, facilitates cross learning of best practices among the artisans of different states and forges lasting business links. Every purchase here supports a rural family," said Dr. Pathania. Himachal Pradesh, the host state, will have 14 stalls representing districts across the state. Products include: Producer groups from Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Jammu & Kashmir, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Haryana and Punjab will bring GI-tagged and traditional products, including: The Mahotsav is part of NABARD's efforts to provide rural producers direct marketing platform. It brings producers, buyers and institutions together in one place and gives GI-tagged and traditional crafts wider visibility. The event supports the national vision of Vocal for Local and Viksit Bharat @2047 and marks the International Year of the Woman Farmer 2026 by showcasing women-led SHGs and enterprises.

headline: Himachal Pradesh: Villagers Oppose TCP Jurisdiction Extension in Rural Areas
content: In Himachal Pradesh, a growing protest is emerging from rural communities against the state government's decision to extend the jurisdiction of the Town and Country Planning (TCP) Department to their areas. The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has announced a rally in Nagri near Palampur on November 17 to voice opposition, alleging that the move imposes undue hardships on villagers.Information was available with The Chenab Times indicating that residents from approximately a dozen gram panchayats are expected to participate in the upcoming rally. The core of their grievance lies in the extension of TCP regulations, which they argue are ill-suited for the rural landscape and its inhabitants. The BJP has adopted this issue, asserting that the government's policy has inadvertently complicated the lives of those residing in villages.The state government had, in 2025, expanded the purview of the TCP Department to encompass several rural territories surrounding Palampur. This expansion, intended to streamline development and planning, has instead ignited considerable resentment among the local populace. Residents have consistently voiced their objections to the imposition of urban-centric town planning norms in what they consider their traditional village settings.Locals claim that the new framework necessitates obtaining approval of site plans from TCP authorities for any construction or renovation projects, whether for houses, shops, or other structures. They contend that this process introduces a labyrinth of additional formalities, often leading to significant delays and increased expenses. This, they argue, makes even straightforward construction activities a formidable challenge for rural families, many of whom are not accustomed to such bureaucratic procedures.The argument put forth by the villagers is that individuals residing in rural areas, often possessing limited financial means, should not be subjected to the same stringent regulatory requirements as those applicable in established urban centres or specifically planned development zones. They feel that the existing infrastructure and lifestyle in villages do not warrant the imposition of these urban planning standards, which are designed for different socio-economic and spatial contexts.While the opposition to the TCP extension remains firm among a significant section of the rural population, local authorities have sought to address some of the concerns. The Palampur Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM), OP Yadav, stated that the government had indeed relaxed certain stringent provisions. He clarified that for constructions such as cowsheds, which are vital for agricultural livelihoods in rural settings, no TCP approval is required. This relaxation, according to the SDM, aims to mitigate some of the perceived hardships faced by villagers in their day-to-day activities and agricultural practices.However, these assurances have not entirely assuaged the fears of many residents. The primary concern revolves around the perceived bureaucratic hurdles and the potential for increased costs associated with any significant building activity. The extended jurisdiction means that any deviation from standard village structures, or any plans for commercial or semi-permanent constructions, would fall under TCP scrutiny. This introduces a level of oversight that many villagers feel is intrusive and unnecessary for their way of life.The extension of TCP jurisdiction into rural areas is a complex issue, often stemming from efforts to manage urban sprawl and ensure planned development across a state. In Himachal Pradesh, a state known for its scenic beauty and developing tourism sector, such measures are often implemented with the intention of preserving the environment and managing infrastructural growth. However, the implementation and communication of these policies play a crucial role in their reception by the local population.The opposition from the rural communities, galvanized by political parties like the BJP, highlights a common tension between top-down development policies and the on-ground realities of rural life. For many villagers, the land they inhabit and the structures they build are intrinsically linked to their livelihood and heritage. Introducing regulatory frameworks designed for urban environments can thus be perceived as an imposition that disrupts established practices and economic activities.The upcoming rally in Nagri is expected to draw a considerable number of participants, underscoring the intensity of local opposition. The BJP plans to use this platform to consolidate its position as a voice for the rural populace against what they term as the state government's anti-people policies. The outcome of this protest and the government's response will be keenly watched, as it pertains to the broader debate on development models and their compatibility with the unique socio-economic fabric of rural India, particularly in ecologically sensitive regions like Himachal Pradesh.

headline: BJYM Himachal Pradesh to hold State Working Committee meeting in Palampur on November 18
content: Shimla (Himachal Pradesh) [India], November 16 (ANI): Sunny Shukla, State President of Bharatiya Janata Yuva Morcha (BJYM), Himachal Pradesh, on Monday, announced that an important State Working Committee Meeting of BJYM Himachal Pradesh will be held on November 18, 2026, in Palampur, keeping in view the upcoming Assembly elections. Senior leadership of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), Himachal Pradesh, will be present at the meeting to guide and motivate the office-bearers and workers of the Yuva Morcha.According to a press release issued by the BYJM, Shukla informed that the meeting will be attended by all State Office-Bearers, State Working Committee Members, District In-Charges, District Presidents and General Secretaries of all organisational districts, along with BJYM Assembly In-Charges and Mandal Presidents representing all 68 Assembly constituencies of Himachal Pradesh. The objective is to prepare the organisation to effectively address upcoming political and organisational challenges and strengthen its presence across the state.He stated that detailed discussions will be held on the strategy for the upcoming Assembly elections, organisational expansion, strengthening the party's presence at the booth level, increasing youth participation, and effectively utilising social media and digital platforms. The meeting will also focus on exposing the failures of the Congress government in Himachal Pradesh, its unfulfilled electoral promises, issues concerning youth employment, unemployment, alleged stagnation in development activities and other public-interest concerns affecting different sections of society.The State President said that despite the passage of considerable time since assuming office, the Congress government has failed to adequately address several important concerns of the people. The youth are still seeking answers on employment opportunities, the pace of development and the promises made before the elections. BJYM will not remain silent on these issues and will hold the state government accountable through facts, public concerns and democratic political engagement.He further made it clear that BJYM will launch an effective statewide political campaign against the policies and functioning of the Congress government. The proposed campaign will include public outreach programmes, Yuva Samvad initiatives, press conferences, demonstrations, social media campaigns and awareness drives at district, mandal and Assembly constituency levels. The organisation will also actively highlight the achievements and welfare initiatives of the Central Government under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.Shukla emphasised that the coming electoral year presents an important opportunity for BJYM to strengthen its organisational capabilities, political outreach and public support. Every Yuva Morcha worker must work with dedication, discipline and commitment to strengthen the BJP's ideology and bring the failures of the Congress government before the people of Himachal Pradesh.He appealed to all designated office-bearers and organisational representatives to ensure their participation in the State Working Committee Meeting at Palampur and contribute actively towards shaping the organisation's future roadmap. (ANI)

headline: Gillette India approves grooming unit shift to Bhiwadi with ₹60 crore capex
content: [Gillette India Limited](https://scanx.trade/company/gillette-india-ltd) has approved the consolidation of its grooming manufacturing operations at Bhiwadi, Rajasthan. This strategic move involves relocating units from Baddi, Himachal Pradesh, to build a more resilient and agile supply chain. The board approved the plan on November 17, 2026, citing long-term strategic vision for sustainable growth. The phased relocation will transfer employees and machinery over approximately 18 to 24 months from the date of disclosure. ## Financial implications The consolidation entails significant upfront costs alongside projected ongoing savings. The company disclosed the following financial impact over the next 2 to 3 years: | Metric | Amount | Nature | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | Capital investment | ₹60 crore | Capex | | One-time expense | ₹100 crore | Relocation cost | | Annual savings | ₹20 crore | Ongoing benefit | The one-time expense covers the costs associated with the transition, while the capital investment supports the new infrastructure in Rajasthan. The projected annual savings are expected to materialize on an ongoing basis post-consolidation. ## Strategic rationale The company stated that the shift aims to create a more resilient, sustainable, and agile supply chain. By centralizing grooming manufacturing at the Bhiwadi unit, Gillette India seeks to optimize operational efficiency. The transfer includes both human resources and physical assets from the Himachal Pradesh facility.

headline: DA hike, arrears: Protest by Himachal Pradesh Road Transport pensioners to be held on 27 Nov. What are they demanding?
content: DA hike, arrears: Pensioners of the Himachal Road Transport Corporation (HRTC) are protesting against the state government for fulfilment of a number of pending demands, including hike in dearness allowance and arrears for previous increase, according to an ANI report.In a statement, Dev Raj Thakur, President of the Transport Pensioners Welfare Association, Himachal Pradesh said that the demands are not excessive and pensioners are “merely seeking parity with what the state government has already provided to other pensioners”, it added.“Serving employees have been granted a 3% DA along with their arrears, whereas we were given the 3% DA without any arrears… The government must find a resolution to this,” Thakur explained. He added that the protestors plan to lay siege (gherao) to the corporation’s headquarters on 27 November.Why are HRTC pensioners protesting? Earlier on 12 November, HRTC pensioners staged a protest outside the office of the corporation’s Managing Director in Shimla and accused the state of failing to fulfil its assurances made ahead of Diwali, as per the report. They also sought fulfilment of long-pending financial demands. Protesting under the banner of the HRTC Pensioners Welfare Association and the HP Pensioners Joint Action Committee, they have alleged discriminatory treatment of retired employees, particularly regarding DA, pension arrears and other retirement benefits. Brij Lal Thakur, Media in-charge of the HRTC Pensioners JAC in Himachal Pradesh, said pensioners had been struggling to receive their dues for the past four years, but neither the state government nor the corporation management had seriously addressed their concerns.He said pensioners had been protesting despite their advanced age and difficult weather conditions. Their main demand was that HRTC pensioners should receive the same benefits as other state government pensioners.What are demands raised by HRTC pensioners?Thakur said the organisation had 16 demands, with the main being that HRTC pensioners are provided the same benefits as state government pensioners. According to him, pensioners were seeking the following:Implementation of financial orders issued by the Finance Department, including pension revision benefits and additional pension allowances of 5%, 10% and 15% for those aged 65, 70 and 75 years, respectively.“Thousands of cases related to these benefits were still pending, even after pensioners had approached the tribunal, High Court and Supreme Court over nearly 14 years,” he stated.He further alleged that arrears under the Assured Career Progression (ACP) scheme, pending since the tenure of former Chief Minister Virbhadra Singh, had also not been cleared.He also questioned the government’s decision to grant only a 3% DA increase to HRTC pensioners, as their demand was for an 8% increase, in line with the benefits sought by other state pensioners.He added that the government has also failed to clear pending arrears, claiming that the outstanding dues amounted to hundreds of crores of rupees.Referring to the recent High Court directions on the payment of pension-related arrears, Thakur welcomed the decision and urged the government to release the first instalment by December 15 and the second by February 28, 2027, along with interest.Pensioners to intensify protests?He warned that pensioners would intensify their agitation and gherao legislators, ministers, Deputy Chief Minister and Chief Minister if their demands remained unresolved. He also threatened protests in Haroli, the constituency of Deputy Chief Minister Mukesh Agnihotri, and Nadaun, represented by Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu.Thakur said HRTC had approximately 8,700 pensioners and around 12,000 serving employees, adding that of these, nearly 11,000 retired employees and around 8,500 pensioners were associated with the organisation. He warned that the agitation would be intensified if the government failed to respond to their demands.Pensioners from across Himachal Pradesh would gather in Shimla on 27 November, with their families to continue the agitation and gherao the HRTC headquarters, he added.The protest on Friday was part of a wider agitation being organised by pensioners across the state over their pending financial and retirement-related demands.(With inputs from ANI)

headline: One girl dies, another missing after jumping into stream in Himachal’s Bilaspur
content: Shimla, Nov 16 (PTI) One girl died and another was missing after they allegedly jumped into a stream in Himachal Pradesh’s Bilaspur when their families found out that the two friends had left home on the pretext of appearing for an exam, police said on Monday. According to police, the two girls informed their families on Saturday that they were going to Sundernagar for an exam. However, on Sunday, their families came to know that both of them were in Ghumarwin. Then their family members also went there. Upon seeing their family members, the two girls jumped into the stream and were swept away by the strong current. After being informed by locals, police reached the spot and launched a rescue operation along with fire department personnel. With the help of the locals, the teams were able to recover the body of one of the girls, which was taken to a nearby hospital. Bilaspur Superintendent of Police Abhishek Dhiman said the search for the second girl is underway. PTI COR DIV This report is auto-generated from PTI news service.
